extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants / principal investigators / research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes NOT-OD-26-012 emergency changes to NIH peer review feedback and what applicants should expect and do (tiering of applications, new summary statement format, and implications for resubmission and funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered review grouping (three tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review meetings will group applications into three tiers: top third (approx. 30–35%), middle third, and bottom third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the traditional model of roughly 50% discussed. The change is intended to clear backlog and preserve fairness while simplifying meetings. It is an emergency modification effective January 2026 through May 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top third — discussed and fully considered for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately the top 30–35% of applications will be discussed openly during study section and will receive full summary discussion and consideration for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For discussed applications, overall impact scores will continue to be reported. Being in this tier preserves the prior level of visibility and detailed meeting discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle third — 'competitive but not discussed' (eligible for funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications in the middle third will be labeled 'competitive but not discussed'; they will not be discussed in the meeting but remain eligible for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not discussed, these applications are still considered by Institutes/Centers and can be funded based on programmatic priorities. Applicants in this band should treat critiques as actionable and consider resubmission strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bottom third — 'not competitive' with limited feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The bottom third of applications will be designated 'not competitive' and will not be discussed; they will receive limited feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited visibility and reduced actionable feedback mean applicants may need to rely on reviewer critiques, PO conversations, and substantial revision before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement format change (simplified, less narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements will no longer use paragraph discussion; instead they'll include a short sentence on committee consensus plus bullet points explaining key scored elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative discussion is reduced. Expect concise committee-consensus language and discrete bullets tied to scored elements rather than long-form paragraph summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer critiques retained (three assigned reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will still receive the written critiques from their three assigned reviewers alongside the simplified summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These written critiques are emphasized as the primary source of detailed reviewer feedback to guide resubmission and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score reporting limited to discussed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall impact scores will be reported for applications that are discussed (top tier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is 'competitive but not discussed' or 'not competitive', overall impact scores may not be provided in the same way, reducing that numerical signal for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic consideration affects funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutes and Centers will weigh programmatic priorities alongside scores when making funding decisions, including for applications not discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align proposals with NIH strategic interests and engage program officers, because funding can hinge on programmatic fit as well as peer review tiering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant actions for producing stronger resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use written critiques to sharpen resubmissions, align proposals with NIH strategic interests, and consult program officers for guidance and interpretation of feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the new feedback structure as a roadmap for improvement rather than an obstacle. Proactive PO engagement and strategic realignment can increase chances of moving into the discussed tier on future submissions.
